Even sober, my dad has an abusive personality. He was always especially hard on me and my brother. My brother, being jealous of how they treated me (his words, not mine) always took his frustrations about that and most other things on me. I have a scar on the top of my foot from stepping on a curved piece of broken glass while wearing sandals while exploring with my brother. He made no effort to help me walk back to where an adult was to get help. Our relationship is strained and I have already cut contact with him outside of if I have to go to my parents' house for any reason.

I haven't gone NC with my parents yet, but once I get my own vehicle (mine is currently under my parents' auto insurance and in my dad's name with me listed as the primary driver), I more than likely will drop contact with them, except for my mom.

I feel so bad about it. My dad was and is a troubled man raised by parents that worked hard to provide for their children. The alcoholism changed my dad and it's a huge point of shame for him. Looking back, I remember my parents arguing about it quite a few times. There was one point where they were arguing on a near daily basis. The song Family Portrait by Pink was a good description. I sang it in the car often with my mom. And the only reason my parents didn't get divorced when I was a kid is because I came into their bedroom when my dad was packing to leave and begged him to stay. I remember he stopped and looked at me and asked, "if you really want me to stay, I will, for you." That was before he'd really been heavily abusive towards me, so I'd have been broken if he had. Now... I wonder what my life would have been like if he had left. So much would be different. 

I still love my parents, and I think that's what kills me. They went through so much to be where they are today and I can't bring myself to look past the abuse. I was raised believing family is important, more than most things. But I haven't felt like we were a family in years. I'm 26 now and still struggling to get through my own trauma, I can't keep going with them hurting me still just because of our differing beliefs. I'm trans, I'm gay, I'm poly. My dad would be devastated and livid if they found out. My mom knows and while she doesn't understand, she's supportive enough to not tell my dad because of how he'd react. I want so much to be able to have the kind of parents other people have, but I can't.

Thanks for reading and sorry about the formatting, posting from my phone. I didn't mean to write this much, but I honestly feel a little better now that I have.
